procedure: P5a step 4, 2026-11-21, following virtualgamepad issue #154 comment 6609886559. vg SHA ed8065b4be2c266dd64e9cedba16e87889392a14. Linux 7.3.0-1-mainline. One operator-owned DualSense confirmed by a physical USB ancestor. The test opened hidraw13 with stock playstation bound throughout. Kernel or other consumer LED writes could confound visual effects. Anders reported the visual observations after each 63-byte USB output 0x02. Valid flag 0 stayed zero. The runner wrote only the step-specific LED bits in valid flags 1 and 2 and their payload fields. No device-originated bytes were collected. Repeated the paired single-bit patterns, mute value 1, and three off/on cycles in each player LED transition mode. Sent a final LED-only restore and confirmed the blue lightbar, one centre player LED and mute LED off. The driver stayed bound and the descriptor was closed.
semantic_outcome: L1. RGB (255,0,0), (0,255,0) and (0,0,255) appeared red, green and blue respectively. L2. setup 0x02 turned the lightbar off by the observation. Transition timing was not measured. L3. 0x04 lit the centre. 0x02 and 0x08 each appeared to light two near-centre positions, and 0x01 and 0x10 each appeared to light two outer positions, also on repeat. The observer could not distinguish the sides within either pair, so single-bit position mapping remains unresolved. L4. 0x04, 0x0A, 0x15, 0x1B, and 0x1F appeared as centre only, inner pair, centre plus outer pair, inner and outer pairs, and all five respectively. L5. with 0x20 clear, the repeated off-to-on transition was gentle and visibly faded in; with 0x20 set the on transition was immediate. Off transitions looked immediate in both modes. L6. value 0 was off, value 1 was initially reported off and was solid on repeat, and value 2 pulsed. L7. with 0x1F selected, the observer saw no brightness difference among 0, 1 and 2. L8. release alone turned the mute and player LEDs off and left the lightbar on in cyan. These are observations on one unit, with stock driver writes a possible confound and no photometric or timing measurements.
